sections.h2: Who pays closing costs when a Texas house sells?
sections.html:
The sales contract decides, and in most resale deals the contract is a standard form from the Texas Real Estate Commission. TREC lists its One to Four Family Residential Contract (Resale), Form 20-19, with an effective date of July 1, 2026, and describes it as the most frequently used contract for single-family homes, duplexes, triplexes and fourplexes.

The form does not cover condominiums, new homes sold by a builder, or farm and ranch property. Those use other TREC forms, so a seller of one of those property types should check which contract applies before negotiating. Ask your agent or title company to walk you through the cost paragraphs of whichever form is used, since individual lines can be changed by negotiation.

sections.h2: What does a Texas seller typically see on the closing statement?
sections.html:
Expect charges tied to clearing title and settling the year's taxes, plus anything you agreed to cover in the contract. The items below come from the official pages that describe how Texas closings work.

  • Payoff of any mortgage or other lien, so the lienholder's claim is released at funding.
  • Property taxes for your share of the year, because the lien attaches on January 1 and the buyer cannot get clear title with delinquent taxes outstanding.
  • The owner's title policy premium, if the contract assigns it to you.
  • Escrow, tax certificate and delivery charges, which the Texas Department of Insurance says many title companies add.
  • Recording charges for any release or curative document you must file.
  • Seller concessions, if you agreed to contribute toward the buyer's costs.

Lenders must give buyers a Closing Disclosure three business days before closing, according to the CFPB. A seller can ask the title company for a draft settlement statement in the same window.

sections.h2: Who pays for the owner's title policy in Texas?
sections.html:
The buyer and seller may negotiate it. The Texas Department of Insurance says the premium is paid once at closing, and that the parties can agree on who bears it.

The amount is not negotiable with the title company. TDI says Texas title rates are regulated and that every title company charges the same premium for a given policy. As printed on its FAQ, the basic premium is $496 for a $50,000 property and $832 for a $100,000 property. That page also notes that the premium covers the title search, examination and closing service, so you are not billed separately for those pieces.

Title insurance is not required by Texas law, per TDI, though a lender will require a loan policy. TDI also warns that you may pick any title company, and that RESPA bars a seller from conditioning the sale on a particular insurer.

sections.h2: What should a seller do before closing day to avoid surprises?
sections.html:
Gather the paperwork and questions early, because a Texas closing moves quickly once a contract is signed.

  • Get a payoff letter from each lender with a lien on the property.
  • Ask the escrow officer for a draft settlement statement as soon as one exists.
  • Confirm in writing who pays the owner's policy premium and which escrow fees fall to you.
  • Pull the current tax bill and note the year's due dates.
  • If the property is held by a married couple, confirm both spouses will sign.

Those steps cost nothing and tend to catch errors while there is still time to fix them.

sections.h2: What is the difference between a title commitment and a title policy?
sections.html:
Per TDI, the commitment arrives before closing and the policy is issued afterward. The commitment says the company is willing to insure the buyer on stated conditions, including any problems the seller must fix. It lists potential issues, exclusions and exceptions, and it does not promise that no problem exists.

For a seller, the commitment is the early warning. It can reveal a lien, an unpaid judgment or a gap in the chain of ownership while there is still time to cure it. TDI's list of title defects includes forged or improperly witnessed documents, unrecorded easements, liens for unpaid taxes or association charges, and claims from missing heirs.

Read the commitment as soon as the buyer's title company produces it, and ask the escrow officer which items you are expected to clear. A seller who clears them quickly avoids a delayed funding date.

sections.h2: What other charges can a title company add?
sections.html:
TDI tells consumers that escrow fees differ between companies, and it names tax certificates, escrow, recording and delivery as common add-ons beyond the premium. You may review the closing papers ahead of time and bring a lawyer.

Recording charges follow the Local Government Code schedule that the clerk manual reproduces.

Deed recording charges printed in the 2023 clerk manual
ChargeAmount in the manual
Opening page of an instrument$5.00
Every later page or partial page$4.00
Each name beyond five that must be indexed$0.25

Records technology and infrastructure$2.00

Source: County Clerk Manual, 2023 edition. A missing grantee mailing address may add $25, per the manual. Counties may differ on capped charges, so confirm the current schedule with your clerk.

sections.h2: How do property taxes interact with the sale?
sections.html:
Bills go out around October 1, and the Comptroller says delinquency begins February 1 for most. Penalty and interest accrue from there, and the Comptroller's payment page prints the full schedule.

Because that year's lien attaches on January 1, a closing early in the year can find the prior bill still open. The Comptroller adds that whoever owned on that January date remains liable, even after selling. So request the tax certificate at the start of the process and make sure the payoff covers any unpaid year.

Buyers who take title after January 1 may be able to claim the school homestead exemption for the rest of that year if the seller never held it. Mention that to your buyer.

sections.h2: Is there a Texas transfer tax on the deed?
sections.html:
The sources cited here list recording fees but no state transfer tax. A county clerk records instruments for the county in which the land lies, and the instrument has to be acknowledged or sworn before an authorized officer.

A draft settlement statement shows every government charge before you commit.

sections.h2: Do closing costs change my federal tax result?
sections.html:
They can. The IRS measures gain from your adjusted basis and amount realized, and the Topic 701 exclusion applies to what remains. Publication 523 is the place to learn which selling expenses count. Texas imposes no state income tax, according to the Comptroller, so the question is federal only.

Keep the final settlement statement. The CFPB also notes that some lines are credits and others charges, so read each line, including seller-paid items.

faqs.q: Who pays closing costs when selling a house in Texas?
faqs.a: It depends on the contract. TREC's resale form 20-19 is the most frequently used, and each cost line can be negotiated. Read the cost paragraphs with your agent or title company before signing.

faqs.q: Can I negotiate the title insurance premium in Texas?
faqs.a: No. TDI says the premium is regulated and every title company charges the same amount for a policy. What you can negotiate with the buyer is who pays it, and you can compare escrow and other fees between companies.

faqs.q: Is title insurance required to sell a Texas home?
faqs.a: Texas does not require it, per TDI. A buyer's lender will require a loan policy, and buyers often purchase an owner's policy as well. The contract says who pays for it.

faqs.q: What are the recording fees for a Texas deed?
faqs.a: The 2023 clerk manual prints $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, plus capped records fees. Counties differ on some charges, so get today's schedule from the clerk.

faqs.q: Will I owe property tax at closing if I sell in the spring?
faqs.a: Possibly. The lien attaches each January 1 and most bills are delinquent after January 31, so the prior year must be paid and the current year divided between you and the buyer. The settlement statement shows the split.
